items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: So we used to go down to places where Jimmy Noon was working on the Paradise.

ctx.x: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I wasn't working with the New Orleans Rhythm Kings, I was working on Clark Street. And I'd be down to New Orleans Rhythm Kings, Mike Frenzel, if they'd get off early, we'd go out to where Joe was working and sit around and listen. And by the fact, we started out originally as a cornet team. Oh, would you talk about that a little? I didn't know that. Well, sure. I was working at the Vista dance hall on 43rd Street three nights a week. Vytavec used to come out with me. I used to get…

He was working in Chicago on Charlie Strait. This was the winter of 22. He had a Peewee with him, a drum boy. He had a band at the Arcade in St. Louis on the Alice Street. Well, he was around 22. He was in Chicago. The winter of 22. No, he was in Chicago then.

items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: Jimmy Noon was in the band. There was a four-piece band and Teddy Weatherford was playing the piano.

ctx.x: Do you remember where you heard Kepler?

Yes, I heard it was a place on 35th Street, I think 35th and Prairie. Jimmy Noon was in the band. There was a four-piece band and Teddy Weatherford was playing the piano. Oh, yeah. And I think Tubby Hall was playing the drums. They used to start about one o'clock in the morning. Because they really hear some music around Chicago then. We're down in New Orleans right now. There's no music down here.
Nothing like there used to be.
